title: Jim White, the contortion drummer
summary: The drummer he replaced juggled and tossed sticks; Moore learned to use nine sticks from him, and explains the showmanship demanded of drummers.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: So you were engaged to play drums, and you played a couple of nights, and was that it? What was the name of the drummer that you replaced? Do you recall his name?
John White...Jim White... No, I say that... His name was Jim White.
Jim White. Tall, nice-looking fellow. That's where I got my inspiration about using so many sticks. He

used to keep sticks in his boots or under his arm when he was playing, you know -- in his mouth. He was what you call a contortion drummer. He tossed the sticks, you know, and [SINGS A RHYTHM] -- all that stuff. You know, he'd reach down and get them. That's when I got that idea. I couldn't use that many sticks, but I got that idea, that pattern(?) in about...oh, about three or four weeks. In fact, I got so I could use nine sticks, just have them placed on the bass drum, and two under my arms, one in my mouth, two in my hands. I'd have to use a chair, like a dinner chair you sit in for your dinner or breakfast... That's the kind of chair you have to use for nine sticks. But what I'm doing now, I'm only...I'm using four sticks now. I've got my own stool, what you call a drum stool, a round stool.
Those drummers were called, as you mentioned, contortion drummers or contortionist drummers?
Were drummers like that very common? Did the average drummer in some of these shows do a lot of these sort of acrobatics, throwing the sticks up in the air and...? Was that the usual...?
Most of that started down South.
I see. This is what the people wanted to see.
They wanted to see that. The first thing they'd do in the band is ...(?)...the drummer. Because the drummer's got to be doing something. He just can't sit up there, you know...
